text: The three masking-profile operations are fixed at GET /admin/masking-profiles, POST /admin/masking-profile-versions and POST /admin/masking-profiles/{roleCode}/unmask on the base /api/recovery/access/v1, with Reference data R for the read, Reference data C for the write and the row's own unmasked flag for the unmask; the consumed ACE-view read of rwb-source-data sits on the P1 base /api/recovery/source-data/v1.
why: No source names a masking-profile operation or its right, while the legacy story needs the profile read, the version write and the unmask; the rights are taken from TSD P4 v3 T6.1 and the base and path rule from DP-13 and the naming rules of the context pack.
read: RWB-AD-004 Endpoints and permission checks; TSD P4 v3 T6.1 and T6.2; context pack P4 (REST base /api/recovery/access/v1, ownership rows); Template and Rules R4 and DP-13
confirm: Solution architect, P4 and the API specification owner at the wave 4 contract review
impact: If the paths or rights differ, both stories change in the metadata-free parts only: the contract document, the fakes and the two REST tables; the profile rows, the version rule and the invariant are unchanged.

text: The unmask read is recorded through the ACE Common audit and PII path (TSD P4 v3 T5.1 INT-22) and the record carries the actor reference, the role code, the field id, the case reference, the masking version and the time; the record is written before the value is answered, so a record that cannot be written answers 503 with MSG-P7-003 and no value.
why: The legacy story requires the read to be written to the PII log and forbids personal data outside it, but no source names the producer, the record name or its fields; the same fail-closed pattern is used for the access log in FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-007-03.
read: RWB-AD-004 AC2; TSD P4 v3 T5.1 INT-22; FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-007-03; NFR-040 and NFR-042
confirm: ACE Common audit and PII logging owner
impact: A producer with a different field list changes the mapper and the PII record fields in the contract only.

text: A masking_rule row carries the field id only, and the view and the column a masked value comes from are resolved from that field id through the P1 field registry at read time; no view-name or column-name column is added to masking_rule.
why: The legacy guardrail says a masking rule names the view column, and TSD P4 v3 T3.1 gives masking_rule no such column, so the two must be reconciled without inventing a column or a value.
read: RWB-AD-004 Guardrails and Data (masking_rule DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-204); TSD P4 v3 T3.1; FSD P4 v3 AC-ALT-P4-004-01 and AC-EXC-P4-004-05
confirm: Data steward, P4 and the P1 field-registry owner
impact: A stored view and column per rule would add a migration and a validation, and would let a profile change name a column the view does not hold.

text: The Compliance approval of a masking-profile version is the reference-load approve gate of RWB-P4-AD010-APP with the approver role RW-COMPLY, and the masking-profile stories write the version and never approve it; the approve right A and the rollback stay with AD010.
why: The legacy AC3 starts from 'a new masking_rule version approved by Compliance' and the legacy permission checks give Reference data A to RW-COMPLY only, while no source gives the masking-profile write its own approve operation.
read: RWB-AD-004 AC3 and permission checks; TSD P4 v3 T6.1 (Reference data A: RW-COMPLY); RWB-AD-010 and RWB-AD-013 in the same master
confirm: Compliance and PDPA officer and the reference-data administrator
impact: One approval path for every versioned reference table, and no second four-eyes implementation for masking.

text: Every read record carries the masking version in force and the field ids with their masked flags, and the access-entry writer of RWB-P4-E1039-APP writes the entry; the masking-profile stories supply the version and the flags and write no access-log row themselves.
why: The legacy AC3 requires the access log to carry the version in force, while the access log is the decision log owned by P7 and written by the E1039 story; the profile story must not duplicate that write.
read: RWB-AD-004 AC3; FSD P4 v3 AC-P4-007-01; TSD P4 v3 T6.1 and T7 NFR-042; DP-03
applied_in: 1 Story; 8 BR5; 9 State transitions; 15 Screens and states; 16 TC-AD-004-03
confirm: Compliance and PDPA officer and the access-log owner
impact: The access log stays one append-only ledger, and a masking change is provable from the log without a second store.

text: rwb-access publishes no business event for this capability: the only publication is the decision-record message of the local library on rwb.decision-record.v1, and a masking change reaches a consumer on the profile read and on the access log; a version in force is never edited, and the earlier version is closed with valid_to set to the day before the later valid_from.
why: The P4 ownership rows give the service no event, so a masking-change event would be an invented name; the version rule comes from TSD P4 v3 T4 and LOV-VERSION-STATUS, which fix the states but not the closing date.
read: Context pack P4 ('Events (0)', ownership rows, DP-03, DP-09); TSD P4 v3 T4 and T3.2 LOV-VERSION-STATUS; RWB-AD-004 AC3
confirm: Solution architect, P4 and the event platform owner
impact: A consumer that needs to refresh on a profile change polls the profile read or reads the access log; if an event is later required, it is added as a new contract element and not as a rename.
